subject: ERPs + Prepaid Ladder: PO schema and net-term sprint
messages:
From: Michael Barnes <michael.barnes@helixhealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@helixhealth.com
Date: 2027-11-10T17:02:00-08:00
Subject: Inquiry on PO fields, monthly invoicing and prepaid discount ladder

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to check a few details before we proceed to finalize the SOW:

- Our AP team requires the PO to include an explicit GL_account, BU_code, and remit_to address. Can Redwood accept a PO with those fields?
- We prefer monthly invoicing aligned to calendar month rather than weekly statements. Is that supported?
- We are interested in a prepaid commitment ladder (quarterly prepay with a 6-month lookback) tied to a discount band. Would Redwood be open to front-loading a portion of the discount on the first invoice if we commit to a 12-month annual spend band?

I attached our PO template for reference. If it helps, we can set up a short call with procurement and AP.

Thanks,
Michael Barnes
Director, Strategic Sourcing
HelixHealth
procurement@helixhealth.com

Attachment: Helix_PO_Template.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Barnes <michael.barnes@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace OConnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-12T11:18:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Inquiry on PO fields, monthly invoicing and prepaid discount ladder

Hi Michael — thanks, and great to hear procurement is moving. Quick answers and next steps below.

- PO fields: Yes, we can accept a PO with GL_account, BU_code, remit_to, tax_entity, and order_number. We ask that the PO include an allowed billing_contact and a billed_entity match. I attached our recommended PO template which maps Redwood invoice fields to common ERP columns.
- Monthly invoicing: Supported. Our hosted billing system can issue monthly invoices; we can also split invoices by BU if your PO is structured that way.
- Prepaid ladder and discount: We can offer a tiered discount for committed spend. Front-loading a portion of the discount on the first invoice is possible but depends on the payment schedule (prepay vs net terms). Typical play: a small up-front prepayment to secure the top-tier discount, with the remainder invoiced monthly against consumption.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben/Grace and I will review your attached PO template and map required fields to our billing ledger.
2) If you can share the desired net-term (Net30/45/60/90) and whether the PO will be Blanket vs. Single, we will confirm internal approvals and an implementation path.
3) If needed, schedule a 30-min procurement call this week to walk AP through the mapping.

I attached our PO template and the (short) SLA addendum that covers prepay credit handling.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Commercial Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_PO_Template_RequiredFields.xlsx (xlsx), Redwood_SLA_Addendum_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Michael Barnes <michael.barnes@helixhealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@helixhealth.com
Date: 2027-11-13T09:44:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Inquiry on PO fields, monthly invoicing and prepaid discount ladder

Priya — thanks for the thorough note. A few clarifications from our side:

- Net terms: Our standard is Net90 for platform vendors at this commitment level. That is preferred but not absolutely blocking — procurement will raise it as a requirement.
- PO type: Blanket PO covering multiple business units. AP requires each invoice to be tagged with BU_code and split per BU on the invoice PDF (we can provide a sample).
- Front-loaded discount: Procurement wants 40% of the agreed discount to apply to the first invoice (they use that to offset onboarding costs). Rest can be amortized monthly.

I've attached our Helix PO template with notes in column "VendorNotes" to show where our AP team expects values. If Net90 is a hard limit for you, let me know. Otherwise procurement will push for Net90 + monthly splits.

We are flexible on the prepayment cadence if Redwood prefers a partial advance + monthly invoicing.

Mike
Michael Barnes
Director, Strategic Sourcing — HelixHealth
Attachment: Helix_PO_Template.xlsx (re-sent)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Barnes <michael.barnes@helixhealth.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace OConnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-15T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Inquiry on PO fields, monthly invoicing and prepaid discount ladder

Hi Mike — looping in Finance and Ops to align. Appreciate the template and notes. High-level response and one proposal: 

1) Net terms: Net90 is higher than our standard for hosted API deals. We can agree to Net60 as our managed compromise, or Net90 if Helix accepts a staged payment schedule: an initial prepayment (30% of NTD) on contract execution followed by monthly invoices net90 for the remainder. That prepayment lets us begin provisioning and grants the front-loaded discount portion you requested.

2) Blanket PO + invoice splits: We can produce one master monthly invoice that includes discrete line items per BU and a corresponding CSV or PDF breakdown suitable for your ERP. Your AP note about BU_code tagging is fine — we will populate BU_code and GL_account fields on each line.

3) Front-loaded discount: We can allocate up to 50% of the negotiated discount to the first invoice if a 30% prepayment is provided. Otherwise the discount will be amortized over the first three invoices.

Operational asks from Redwood:
- Please ensure the PO includes order_number, remit_to, tax_entity, billed_entity_email, BU_code, and GL_account.
- Sign the attached SLA addendum that documents how prepay credits are applied and refunded for underutilization.

If that approach works for Helix, we will prepare a short amendment and send a DocuSign link. Can we schedule a 30-min call Thursday to finalize?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Billing & Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
